question: What is the primary role of the nurse regarding injection safety?

options.A: Manufacturing sterile needles for hospital pharmacies
options.B: Ensuring every injection follows strict safety standards
options.C: Reporting expired drug batches to federal agencies
options.D: Prescribing the correct medication dosage for patients

explanation: Nurses administer medications directly and carry the professional duty to maintain aseptic technique and prevent harm. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is poor injection safety a major public health threat?

options.A: It can spark community outbreaks of systemic infections
options.B: It primarily causes immediate skin irritation at the site
options.C: It increases the financial cost of purchasing syringes
options.D: It leads to widespread allergic reactions to antiseptics

explanation: Unsafe practices can rapidly transmit blood-borne pathogens from patient to patient, creating wide-scale outbreaks. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h1)

question: What defines an unsafe injection procedure?

options.A: Giving an intramuscular injection in the deltoid muscle
options.B: Any procedure risking harm to the recipient or provider
options.C: Administering clear medications without prior aspiration
options.D: Using a syringe with a retractable safety mechanism

explanation: The clinical definition encompasses any practice that exposes patients or staff to preventable health hazards. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h2)

question: Where do unsafe injection practices most commonly create a heavy disease burden?

options.A: Only during mass vaccination campaigns in urban centers
options.C: In regions facing medical supply shortages and workarounds
options.D: Exclusively within high-tech intensive care units

explanation: Resource constraints frequently lead to dangerous shortcuts like reusing single-use equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is a major danger of using multi-dose medication vials incorrectly?

options.A: The chemical composition of the drug instantly vaporizes
options.B: Pathogens can enter the vial and infect subsequent patients
options.C: The rubber stopper becomes completely impossible to pierce
options.D: Medication expiration dates shorten by several years

explanation: A contaminated needle entering a multi-dose vial introduces microorganisms directly into the shared medication supply. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which scenario describes a severe breach in basic aseptic technique?

options.A: Discarding a used disposable syringe into a puncture-proof box
options.B: Checking the medication label three times prior to withdrawal
options.C: Wiping the patient skin site with a 70 percent alcohol swab
options.D: Touching the sterile shaft of a needle before piercing the skin

explanation: Contact with the sterile portion of injection equipment compromises sterility and introduces skin flora into deep tissues. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which pathogen is known to survive on environmental surfaces for long periods?
explanation: Hepatitis B remains stable and infectious on dry surfaces much longer than many other blood-borne viruses. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h4)

question: How do pathogens from unsafe injections typically enter the human body?

options.A: Through direct vascular or deep tissue inoculation during delivery
options.B: By aerosol inhalation while standing near the medication cart
options.C: Through ingestion of contaminated municipal drinking water
options.D: Via casual skin contact with an infected person clothing

explanation: The needle bypasses normal skin barriers, placing pathogens straight into underlying tissue or bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is a common local complication arising from a contaminated injection site?
explanation: Introduction of pyogenic bacteria directly into tissue pockets frequently leads to localized pus accumulation and abscesses. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which long-term pathology is strongly associated with chronic viral hepatitis transmission?
explanation: Long-standing viral activity in the liver causes scarring and cellular destruction, ending in cirrhosis or cancer. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h5)

question: What physical finding should a nurse specifically look for when assessing previous injection sites?

options.A: Induration or signs of chronic abscesses
options.B: Asymmetrical swelling of the lower limbs

explanation: Prior traumatic or contaminated injections leave local tissue changes like hardness, scarring, or localized infection. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is taking a detailed history of informal healthcare exposures important during evaluation?

options.A: Government agencies require tracking of herbal remedies
options.B: Informal treatments never involve any form of injection
options.C: Unregulated providers may use unsterilized equipment
options.D: Patients always remember the exact brand of syringe used

explanation: Unregulated settings often lack proper infection control oversight, elevating the risk of blood-borne pathogen exposure. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the core golden rule for safe syringe and needle usage?

options.A: Share single-dose vials among three patients
options.B: One needle, one syringe, only one time
options.C: Recap all needles immediately after injection
options.D: Reuse syringes only if washed with hot water

explanation: This universal phrase summarizes the mandate against reusing injection equipment across multiple patients. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice when handling used sharps?

options.A: Placing disposal bins close to the work area
options.B: Recapping used needles using both hands
options.C: Dropping syringes straight into a rigid box
options.D: Avoiding the bending of contaminated needles

explanation: Recapping used needles with two hands dramatically raises the risk of accidental needlestick injuries to the nurse. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h7)
